statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by INPI (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with name and similarity verification against the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) and the INPI trademark database (Data INPI).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin (alphabetic) script and, for an SAS, must be followed by the words 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or the initials 'SAS' and the stated amount of share capital (Art. L.227-4 Code de commerce). All statutory filings and public-facing documents must be in French; foreign-language deeds require certified translation by a court-approved translator (traduction assermentée) in accordance with the Toubon Law (Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994). The name must be distinctive and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS-registered denomination or to a registered trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Crédit / Caisse (regulated credit institution words requiring ACPR authorization)
Bourse / Investissement / Fonds (regulated financial services words)
Avocat / Notaire / Commissaire aux comptes (regulated professional titles)
France / République / National (terms implying state sponsorship or nationality requiring prior authorization)
Trust / Offshore / Fiducie (terms triggering enhanced UBO and AML scrutiny by banks and TRACFIN)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the greffier of the Tribunal de commerce or the INPI Guichet unique, the applicant (i) rectifies the substantive defect and re-submits through the Guichet unique without duplication of fee; (ii) may apply in interim proceedings (référé) to the President of the competent Tribunal de commerce to compel the registrar to proceed with registration where the refusal rests on erroneous name-confusion assessment; (iii) may initiate an action for trademark infringement (contrefaçon) or unfair competition (concurrence déloyale) if the conflicting earlier right is unjustified; and (iv) retains the 30-day name-clearance and legal-publication evidence to support the re-filing. Note: French law does not provide for a formal statutory pre-reservation; priority is fixed by the date of RCS filing, but the 30-day window governs the incorporation announcement and re-filing timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only through a licensed domiciliation provider (société de domiciliation) authorized under Articles L.123-11-1 to L.123-11-7 of the French Code de commerce, evidenced by a written domiciliation contract; a purely virtual letterbox address without genuine administrative substance will be rejected by banks, DGFiP and maritime/industrial site operators for this construction licensing profile.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced administrative on-site inspection risk quantified at 15-20% for the registered office within the first 12 months (DGFiP/URSSAF), rising to 35-40% over a 36-month horizon for a construction-sector SAS; on-site HSE and DREAL safety inspections at LNG receiving terminal work sites are effectively certain (approximately 90%) upon contract mobilization.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) for corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés) and VAT (TVA); e-portal: impots.gouv.fr; company law and registration formalities: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, operated by INPI); customs and export control: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI); non-resident taxpayer liaison: Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French-established SAS: incorporation is filed through the Guichet Unique; INSEE automatically attributes the SIREN (9-digit national tax identification number) and SIRET; the DGFiP allocates the intra-Community VAT identification number (TVA intracommunautaire) on the same registration file; no separate TIN application is required. Non-resident entities: must register for French VAT and tax remittance through the SIEE using Form CERFA 14175 (or standard registration Form CERFA 14171 via the Guichet Unique for entities establishing a permanent establishment); non-EU resident suppliers without a fixed establishment must appoint a VAT fiscal representative (garant) approved by the DGFiP under CGI Art. 289 A. VAT ID format: 'FR' plus 2-digit key plus 9-digit SIREN (11-character intra-Community ID).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope. A French SAS is a separate legal entity mandatorily subject to corporate income tax (IS) under CGI Art. 205, with no pass-through or check-the-box option. France applies the territoriality principle of CGI Art. 209-I: the SAS is taxed on French-source active business profits unless it holds an official authorization to elect worldwide taxation; CIT standard rate 25%, reduced to 15% on the first €42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (CGI Art. 219). No Tax_Exempt_Zone status applies to this metropolitan-France LNG piping activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists in French tax law; classification follows the registered legal form, and an SAS is always IS-taxable (the income-tax option of CGI Art. 239 bis AA is reserved to SARL/EURL only). Available statutory elections: (1) fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under CGI Art. 223 A, allowing a 95%-parent to consolidate French subsidiary results; (2) worldwide aggregation election (régime du bénéfice mondial) under CGI Art. 209 quinquies and global imputation election (régime de l'imputation globale) for foreign branch profits, each requiring DGFiP authorization; (3) hybrid mismatch alignments under ATAD (Directive 2016/1164) implemented via CGI Art. 212 bis, including structured-arrangement rebuttal elections; (4) VAT simplification options including OSS/IOSS registration for intra-EU and non-EU distance sales and the reverse-charge self-invoicing mechanism for inbound B2B construction services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), governed by CGI Arts. 256 to 289 quinquies, transposing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis registration threshold: any French-established taxable person must register for VAT from the first euro of taxable turnover. Small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base de TVA, CGI Art. 293 B) is available below €36,800 annual turnover for services and €91,900 for goods, but this is an exemption, not a registration threshold. Non-established foreign suppliers have no registration threshold; intra-EU distance sales and B2C digital/telecom/broadcasting services trigger registration via the OSS when cross-border turnover exceeds €10,000 per EU-wide calendar year; B2B installation works and cryogenic piping services performed at an LNG terminal in France trigger French VAT registration or reverse charge with no turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting reform (Finance Act 2023 Art. 91; CGI Arts. 289 septies to 289 quindecies): from 1 September 2026 all French taxable persons must receive structured electronic invoices, and large and mid-size enterprises must issue them; from 1 September 2027 PME and micro-enterprises must issue them. Invoices must be exchanged through certified Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires (PDP) or the public Chorus Pro portal using structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII). Transaction data (e-reporting for B2C and intra-EU) is transmitted in real time to the DGFiP through PDP APIs; mandatory invoice data fields follow CGI Art. 289. France does not operate an Italian-style pre-clearance stamping system; enforceability rests on the mandatory PDP/API digital pipeline, the Fichier des Écritures Comptables (FEC) audit extract, and penalties for e-invoicing non-compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating (exonération avec droit à déduction) applies under CGI Art. 262 ter-I-1° to goods physically exported or consigned outside the EU customs territory within 90 days of supply. Art. 262 ter-II extends 0% treatment to services directly linked to exported goods, including transport, loading, handling, and works performed on goods. Services rendered to non-EU customers are outside the scope of French VAT where effectively used outside France (CGI Art. 259-1°). For this LNG receiving terminal piping scope: fabricated cryogenic pipe and insulation materials exported from France qualify as zero-rated goods; on-site installation and welding services performed within France on French immovables are taxable in France at 20% (CGI Art. 259-2°), while installation and welding performed outside the EU fall outside French VAT territoriality. Claim requires documented proof of physical exit from EU customs territory (ECS), a direct nexus between the exported goods and the alleged zero-rated supply, and, for services, evidence of effective use outside France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane – DAU/ECS) lodged electronically with DGDDI and accepted with validated exit
Bill of Lading (or Through Bill of Lading / CMR / air waybill) evidencing physical departure from the EU customs territory to the non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank documentary evidence, SWIFT MT103/MT202, proving payment and repatriation of the export proceeds to the French entity)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP may retrospectively claw back the zero-rated exemption and deny input VAT deduction where export documentation is absent, incomplete, or fraudulent; reassessed VAT attracts late-payment interest (intérêts de retard, CGI Art. 1727) and the new 30% increase per Finance Act rules where applicable. Penalties under CGI Art. 1729 are 40% for manquement délibéré (deliberate inaccuracy) and 80% for manœuvres frauduleuses or abus de droit (fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of law). Sham export arrangements may be recharacterized under LPF Art. L64, exposing the company to the 80% penalty plus loss of the exemption; falsified customs declarations additionally trigger customs fines under Code des douanes Arts. 414 and 426 (fine up to 250% of the evaded duties and possible seizure of goods) and criminal tax prosecution under CGI Art. 1741 (up to €500,000 fine and five years imprisonment for tax fraud). The reassessment limitation period extends to six years for undisclosed or falsely documented transactions (LPF Art. L. 169) and up to ten years where criminal fraud is established; corporate directors may incur joint and several liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the national competent authority for foreign exchange equilibrium, balance-of-payments reporting, and prudential oversight under Articles L.151-1 through L.165-1 and R.151-1 et seq. of the French Code monétaire et financier (CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a fully liberalised current and capital account regime within the eurozone and vis-à-vis non-EU states, consistent with Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. The euro is freely convertible, and no exchange control approval is needed for trade settlement, dividends, capital contributions, or liquidation proceeds in a French SAS. Profit remittance hurdles are not exchange-control-driven; they arise from (i) corporate-law solvency checks on distributions under Article L.232-11 of the French Commercial Code, (ii) tax documentation and withholding tax for non-resident shareholders under Article 119(2) of the CGI (reduced by tax treaty), and (iii) banks' AML-based due diligence requiring clean UBO and sanction-screen status. No routine FX quota, no surrender requirement, and no convertibility restriction should be expected.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: French law does not impose a statutory surrender obligation, a mandatory conversion ratio, or a prescribed repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Export invoices may be settled in EUR or any freely convertible currency, and the proceeds may be retained in a foreign-currency account at an authorised intermediary bank. However, under the French balance-of-payments regulations, any cross-border remittance of EUR 10,000 or more requires statistical reporting to the Banque de France by the transmitting bank or the entity concerned; the underlying export invoice, customs declaration, and proof of delivery must be retained for at least ten years to support the transaction, and failure to report may result in administrative fines but does not invalidate the payment or transfer title.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW-MEDIUM. French-licensed or European-passthrough electronic money institutions and fintech banks, such as Qonto, Pliant, or Mano, can open operational payment accounts, accept SEPA/SEPA Instant credits, and provide basic FX rail for small-to-mid ticket disbursements. Their legal constraint is that an EMI is not a credit institution and therefore cannot issue or confirm documentary letters of credit, provide trade finance guarantees, or hold escrow balances for a capital increase requiring bank attestation. Additionally, many EMIs have low subledger transaction caps for high-value cross-border wiring and lack direct SWIFT membership, causing them to rely on sponsor banks with added compliance friction. For ISIC 4322 LNG-terminal piping contracting, use an EMI for short-term euro float only; run capital escrow and trade settlement through a full-service tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SAS engaged in critical LNG receiving terminal piping works, tier-1 banks normally require at least one director or a duly authorised officer to attend a live KYC/identity interview; this may be carried out by video conference under the bank's digital onboarding policy, but in practice most major banks and enhanced-diligence policies prefer an in-person meeting or an on-site verification visit to the registered office and construction yard. Remote account opening without any direct contact is generally unavailable for this risk category. The French UBO register obligations (Articles L561-46, R561-20 et seq., CMF) require clear identification of natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; apostilled powers of attorney with sworn French translation will be accepted for overseas representatives, but the compliance officer still expects a direct video or physical interview with the controlling director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hit or negative news on a non-resident shareholder, supplier, or underlying goods intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified UN/EU/OFAC sanctions list screenings dated within 30 days; full corporate ownership chart to natural persons; sworn statement of non-circumvention under CMF Article R.561-11; passports and legal existence certificates of all screening subjects; tax residence certificates; French counsel legal opinion clearing any apparent match; and a detailed narrative explaining the commercial nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Enhanced scrutiny due to the LNG receiving terminal qualifying as sensitive national infrastructure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Port authority or government concession award documents; project-specific security clearance permits; ISO 3834 Part 2 certification for welding of cryogenic piping; ISO 9001 quality management certificate; OPQIBI qualification for piping installation (e.g., 1110/1120); insurance certificates for installation, pollution, and equipment; and a security-cleared list of site personnel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid layering of a large inbound capital injection into multiple outbound trade disbursements without clear commercial logic
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cashflow waterfall model approved by the executive board; executed procurement contracts, purchase orders, and vendor invoices; balance-of-payments-relevant narratives on wire instructions; notarised capital contribution deed or shareholder current-account agreement; statutory auditor's certificate if the SAS is mid-size; and monthly project progress report supported by site documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque beneficial ownership structure formed by layered non-resident holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully populated French Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs filed with the Registry of the Commercial Court; top-to-bottom shareholding chart; certified true copies of constitutional documents; sworn UBO declaration identifying each natural-person shareholder; PEP status analysis with source-of-wealth dossier; and notarised powers attorney authorising bank verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fraud or Ponzi red flags around advance payments to overseas suppliers of specialty cryogenic steel or insulation materials
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentary letter of credit or standby LC in favour of the supplier; bank guarantee from a correspondent of the supplier; construction-all-risks insurance policy; pre-shipment inspection certificate; independent quantity surveyor's report; site diary with photographs; and proof of customs declaration progression through the Single Administrative Document.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires a SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfer in EUR, initiated by the foreign shareholder's credit institution, into the SAS's dedicated Capital Escrow Account at a tier-1 French bank. The wire must carry an explicit balance-of-payments purpose code used by the Banque de France, typically the category corresponding to equity participation or shareholder current account (the bank will map the transaction to category such as '1120' acquisition of participations or '7000' loans/current-account advances), together with a clear narrative such as 'APPORT DE CAPITAL SOCIAL - FRANCE SAS - LNG PIPING PROJECT'. Pre-funding verification requires a notarised or legalised capital increase deed, board resolution, Kbis extract, UBO declaration, evidence of source of funds from the sending bank, and CRS/FATCA tax attestations. The receiving bank will file the balance-of-payments report with Banque de France, and the escrowed funds become available after AML/Sanctions clearances; ensuring accurate purpose-code classification and maintaining full underlying documentation avoids frozen funds and reclassification risk. Non-EU parent wires may be in USD and settled through a US correspondent bank using an MT103 cover; the French bank will require the USD,EUR conversion to be made only through its own treasury or a pre-approved FX line.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For procurement of cryogenic stainless steel pipes, valves, insulation, and welding consumables, the primary clearing rails are (i) SEPA credit transfer for EUR payments within the EEA, (ii) SWIFT MT103 for direct vendor wires outside the EEA, and (iii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit opened at a tier-1 bank in favour of suppliers, issued via SWIFT MT700 and governed by UCP 600. Settlement under an LC occurs against presentation of an original bill of lading, signed inspection certificate, packing list, commercial invoice, and, where applicable, EU dual-use export-control documentation. The French bank will require an underlying trade-invoice and contract consistent with the SAS's declared ISIC 4322 activity; the contractor's own import and export must be matched with the Single Administrative Document and TARIC controls. For high-value disbursements, an advance-payment bond or performance bond in favour of the supplier is commonly used; require national bank sanctions screening on the beneficiary bank and ensure each MT103 references the project ID and purpose code to ease Banque de France post-reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla forward foreign exchange contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for firm and forecast trade payables or receivables with a maturity not exceeding 12 months.
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) to hedge principal and interest flows on trade financing and capital expenditure.
European-style FX options, both calls and puts, for procurement contracts with uncertain timing or quantities, settled by physical delivery.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to currencies that are non-fully convertible or have no deliverable onshore FX market, provided the counterparty and settlement currency are consistent with EU sanctions regulations and the bank's internal policy.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) in EUR/USD where the underlying debt or commercial obligation is itself linked to a defined project contract or fixed asset.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and filing of annual accounts with the Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the INPI single business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after the financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and daily penalties may apply; failure to file may trigger a fine of EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat breaches. Prolonged non-compliance may result in registry radiation after formal notice and applicable procedural periods; there is no universal automatic strike-off deadline

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, including Form 2065 and annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December; electronic filing is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally accrues at 0.20% per month, with a standard 10% surcharge for late filing or payment; higher surcharges may apply for serious or repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax compliance and payment for Contribution Foncière des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual payment generally due by 15 December; an annual return is not normally required unless requested or relevant establishment information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and collection surcharges may apply; the amount is assessed according to the cadastral rental value, municipality, and applicable exemptions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the competent Commercial Court through the INPI single business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual confirmation is required; changes to beneficial ownership or control information generally must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare or maintain accurate beneficial ownership information may lead to court injunctions, criminal penalties for responsible persons, and restrictions affecting registry compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional appointment requirements may apply to certain parent, subsidiary, or controlled-company structures.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) General Accounting Plan. IFRS may apply to consolidated accounts or where legally permitted and elected.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation. The SAS must maintain accurate ownership and control information, update its beneficial owner filing within 30 days of a relevant change, and update its securities movement register, shareholder accounts, and corporate records for each share transfer. The legal entity must also confirm information when required by a registry, tax authority, bank, or other regulated intermediary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register or records of shareholder decisions and management decisions
Minutes and attendance records for collective decisions where applicable
Current corporate officer and beneficial ownership records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 600-2,000 per year for registered-office, corporate secretarial, and statutory correspondence services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000-15,000 per year for a small or medium-sized SAS requiring a statutory audit; complex industrial, group, or regulated operations may exceed this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% headline rate with R&D tax credit (30% on first €100k eligible expenses, 5% thereafter), innovation status benefits, and sector-specific deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultat (Form 1204) via impots.gouv.fr electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 March for calendar year ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French-source income only; non-residents without PE report on separate basis

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable operating expenses, depreciation, and provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: TP adjustments and arm's length pricing must be documented
Include only French permanent establishment income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 0.5% of tax due per month of delay (max 25%); non-filing: criminal penalties and tax reassessment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC (Certificat de résidence fiscale) and French withholding tax form to claim DTA reduced rate; process via impots.gouv.fr or bank
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% under most DTAs (domestic rate 25%); Interest: 0% under most DTAs (domestic rate 75%)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million intra-group transactions for local file; €750 million consolidated revenue for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies substance requirements under DAC6 and anti-avoidance rules; limited direct ESR applicability for operating entities but mandatory for holding companies lacking real economic activity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to 500% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and confiscation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, disqualification from corporate offices, and possible travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining French entity without economic substance or genuine business purpose
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of intra-group transactions, denial of deductions, and penalties up to €10 million or 5% of turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil, civil restitution orders, and potential imprisonment for willful misconduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation or engage in aggressive planning without arm's length substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €10 million or 5% of annual turnover, plus criminal sanctions for aggravated cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment, and disqualification; directors may face joint and several liability
